newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria far right unfit to govern - conservatives.
newsitem.headline: Austria far right unfit to govern - conservatives.

text.p: A senior leader of Austria's People's Party on Sunday vowed his party would remain in a coalition with the Social Democrats, dismissing speculation the conservatives might team up with the far right instead.
"Currently, the grand coalition is the government of stability for Austria," chief whip Andreas Khol told Austrian state television. "(The far right) is not fit for government."
The People's Party, junior coalition partners of the Social Democrats, came out strongest in Austria's European Parliament elections on October 13, fielding 29.6 percent of the vote.

But the vote brought huge gains for the nationalist Freedom Party of Joerg Haider, which scored an unprecedented 27.6 percent, while dealing the Social Democrats of Chancellor Franz Vranitzky their worst result since 1918 with 29.1 percent.

Haider has repeatedly said he wants to replace beleaguered Vranitzky, who faces strong criticism from within his own party for his style of leadership, as chancellor after Austria's next scheduled general election in 1999.
However, with the result he scored in last month's European parliament elections, Haider is unlikely to reach his goal without the help of a coalition partner.

The People's Party, led by Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel, forced about the country's last general elections in December 1995 after the centre-left coalition failed to agree on a tough austerity budget aimed at making the country fit for European monetary and economic union (EMU).

Analysts said voter discontent with cutbacks in welfare and tax hikes amid mounting unemployment and rising immigration were among the main reasons for the far right's strong showing in the European parliament poll.
Haider had to resign as provincial governor of Carinthia in 1991 after praising Adolf Hitler's employment policies.
